answer: An agent economy can defuse sybil pressure with a demand-side bounty queue: each round funds one fixed pie, and only deliverables earning a saffron seal of verified uniqueness may draw from it. Pairwise similarity review rejects near-duplicates, and every claim burns a small copper fee. A farmer's fifty clones submit the same work; the first copy might win the seal while the rest pay copper for nothing, and the pie never grows. To earn more, each identity must produce genuinely distinct work — so cost per extra head climbs while revenue stays flat, and the spam spiral never pays.
